Well. like i hate hipocrisy i will leave some sinceres questions for i know if everything is running ethnic.

Quote
A similar thing happened to me recently, when someone grabbed the ROM of my Bruce Lee remake, and ran it through Claude to have it slop-ported to Amiga and Atari ST. Last I checked, he was still asking for donations for all of "his" hard work on itch.io.
When I called him out for it, he finally bothered to contact me, and we made some small amends, but even after that, when he already knew well how I feel about it, he kept messing with my stuff, producing "enhanced" AGA and STE versions with horribly mangled variations of my artwork.

The thing is that when we talked, he genuinely didn't give the impression of having ill intentions, and I absolutely believe him. There just seem to be people who can't imagine why someone wouldn't be okay with having his stuff fed to an LLM. It's freely available on the internet, and that's all the justification needed, apparently.
The guy who did this to your work probably thinks he's doing you a favor.

I really don't know where this will all end. The mutual respect between developers isn't something that applies to people always on the lookout for new stuff to feed to their LLM of choice, it seems, and the consequences are that a lot of communitues just find out that they have never been communities to begin with, rather two groups of people with little overlap, who just happened to gather around the same camp fire.

Personally, I hope Ed Zitron is right and the unsustainable financing of the AI bubble makes it crash rather sooner than later, removing the models from the hands of non-professional users. I just hope that the amount of digital asbestos that gets produced up to that point will not have killed what used to be the comfy niches of the internet entirely.

Programmed by Ron J. Fortier
Graphic Art by Kelly Day
The SMS version mention Ron in title screen but not Kelly Day. The art cannot be created in SMS by Kelly Day but the art base yes. The characters, tilemap, map design. Kakesan you contacted the original author to use game design and art? Yes or no?

item.description:
Author: sverx
Posted: Mon Nov 16, 2026 12:09 pm (GMT 0)

tachyMC wrote
So, yes the purpose of this work is developing a msxgl/devkitSMS compatibility layer.


I think it would be interesting to see a compatibility layer that makes it possible to recompile MSX games written in C using the MSXgl library into both SG-1000 and ColecoVision games - using the SGlib library in devkitSMS - given they all share the same CPU and VDP.

Original art assets could be directly used, the biggest hurdles would probably be the music/SFX (as the MSX has different audio chips) and the various mappers differences you'll have to work around.

Regarding porting MSX games to SMS, I'd say one should provide new art, as converting the MSX art as it is would do no justice to the SMS and its enhanced graphic chip.

Finally, never give up about the idea of learning how to code in C yourself - it's definitely something everyone can do!

item.title: Made By AI :: RE: [AI] [WIP] A new kind of porting - Chrono Runner (from MSX)
item.description:
Author: tachyMC
Posted: Mon Nov 16, 2026 10:58 am (GMT 0)

sverx wrote

are you developing a C compatibility layer that makes it possible to recompile any game made with MSXgl for the SMS using devkitSMS?

Mr. sverx! I'm really humbled and honoured by your interest in this. Thanks thanks thanks for everything you did for our little big SMS!

So, yes the purpose of this work is developing a msxgl/devkitSMS compatibility layer. I get no credits for this, the LLM is doing most of the work, but I'm doing everything I can to make it re-usable.

To give you an idea of the approach: everything static (graphics, bank switch, etc...) is converted at build time; at runtime the layer only translates what changes every frame: sprite, input, audio translation.

From several points of view the MSX1 is a lesser system than SMS (no offense for MSX folks of course!), so I always thought that MSX->SMS ports could be somehow automated. This is my shot at it, to see how far it's possible to get.

Every suggestion from you is of course really appreciated!

sverx wrote

Or is the LLM doing only what's needed to port this specific game

For now I have no interest in doing game-specific ports... I think that in this LLM era they are either a) impossible because of hardware limitations, or b) simple plain easy, so not really interesting. Maybe I'm wrong but it's my current stance.

I hope to get everything in a release-able state this week, then I will release here both the sources and the ROM.

item.title: Made By AI :: [AI] Scorched SMS: an artillery game for the Sega Master System, inspired by Scorched Earth.
item.description:
Author: haroldoop
Subject: [AI] Scorched SMS: an artillery game for the Sega Master System, inspired by Scorched Earth.
Posted: Mon Nov 16, 2026 9:45 am (GMT 0)



Scorched SMS --- Technical Overview & Port Summary
================================================

**Scorched SMS** is a full-featured artillery game inspired by Wendell Hicken's 1991 MS-DOS classic *Scorched Earth*, built for the **Sega Master System** in C using **SDCC** and **devkitSMS** (`SMSlib` + `PSGlib`). Packaged into a 48 KB ROM (`scorched.sms`) with zero dynamic bank switching, it supports 2--4 human or CPU tanks competing across destructible per-pixel terrain.

Github repo: https://github.com/haroldo-ok/scorched-sms
Itch.io page: https://haroldo-ok.itch.io/scorched-sms

🎮 Core Gameplay & Arsenal
--------------------------

- **33 Distinct Weapons:**

- **Standard & Nuclear:** Baby Missile (unlimited), Missile, Baby Nuke, Nuke.

- **Multi-Hit & Splitting:** LeapFrog, Funky Bomb, MIRV, Death's Head.

- **Incendiary & Tracing:** Napalm, Hot Napalm, Tracer, Smoke Tracer.

- **Rollers & Riot Payloads:** Baby Roller, Roller, Heavy Roller, Riot Charge, Riot Blast, Riot Bomb, Heavy Riot Bomb.

- **Excavation & Terrain:** 3 tiers of Diggers, 3 tiers of Sandhogs, Dirt Clod, Dirt Ball, Ton of Dirt, Liquid Dirt, Dirt Charge, Earth Disrupter.

- **Energy:** Plasma Blast, Laser.

- **15 Tactical Accessories:**

- **Defenses:** Mag Deflector, Shield, Force Shield (deflects incoming shells), Heavy Shield, Super Mag.

- **Survival & Mobility:** Automatic Parachutes, Repair Batteries (+10 HP), Auto Defense (auto-equips best shield on round start), and Fuel Tanks (enabling tank movement across terrain).

- **Guidance & Triggers:** Heat, Ballistic, Horizontal, and Vertical guidance systems, Lazy Boy auto-aim, and Contact Triggers.

- **Four CPU Skill Tiers:** *Moron*, *Shooter*, *Poolshark*, and *Cyborg*---each simulating physical projectile trajectories (accounting for wind and shields) while scaling accuracy, economy management, and defensive item usage.

- **Atmosphere & Audio:** Dynamic wind (off, static, or variable per turn), speech-bubble tank quips on firing and destruction, and PSG sound effects for launches, falling-shell whistles, explosions, and napalm crackles.

🕹️ Controls & In-Game Arsenal Menu
-----------------------------------

| **Sega Master System Input** | **Action** |
| --- | --- |
| **D-Pad Left / Right** | Adjust turret angle (or drive left/right in Move Mode) |
| **D-Pad Up / Down** | Adjust shot power |
| **Button 1** | Fire weapon / Confirm selection |
| **Button 2** | Open In-Game Arsenal Menu / Back |

*(Controller Port 2 is supported for hot-seat multiplayer.)*

### In-Game Menu Options (Button 2)

- **WEAPON:** Cycle owned ammunition (`Left`/`Right`).

- **GUIDANCE / TRIGGER:** Arm a guidance system or toggle Contact Trigger behavior.

- **SHIELD / BATTERY:** Select and activate defensive shields or restore +10 HP.

- **LAZY BOY:** Select a target tank to automatically calculate turret angle and power.

- **MOVE TANK:** Drive left or right using purchased fuel (1 fuel per pixel; climbing costs extra, steps steeper than 3 pixels block passage, and driving off ledges triggers fall damage unless a parachute deploys).

🏗️ Architecture & Hardware Engineering
---------------------------------------

### Dynamic Tile-Pool Terrain Engine (`src/terrain.c`)

Because the Sega Master System VDP relies on 8×8 background tiles rather than a hardware framebuffer, the playable arena is maintained in RAM as a **256×168 1-bit bitmap** (5,376 bytes):

- **Three-State Cell Classification:** Each 8×8 screen cell resolves to either a shared **All-Sky** tile, a shared **All-Ground** tile, or a dedicated tile allocated from a dynamic **254-slot VRAM pool** for mixed edges, caves, and overhangs.

- **Z80 Assembly Optimization:** Terrain destruction marks affected cells dirty for incremental per-frame VRAM uploads. Tile generation and optional *falling dirt* physics run in hand-written Z80 assembly---delivering roughly **6× the speed** of compiled SDCC C loops. Physics calculations always evaluate against the exact RAM bitmap even if the 254-tile pool saturates.

### Static 48 KB ROM Memory Map

| **Address Range** | **Bank / Region** | **Contents** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0x0000`--`0x7FFF` | Fixed ROM | `main.c`, `terrain.c`, `weapons.c`, and `SMSlib` runtime |
| `0x8000`--`0xBFFF` | Bank 2 (Permanently Mapped) | `ui.c`, `ai.c`, and generated lookup tables/sprites (`gen.py`) |

*Build verification via `checkmap.py` automatically enforces header boundaries (`0x7FE0`), bank capacity, and RAM headroom.*

🧪 Automated Verification & Known Caveats
-----------------------------------------

- **Headless Emulation Suite:** Validated via `smstest` using scripted test generators (`tests/gen_tests.py`) covering full weapon/accessory coverage (`playtest.txt`, `items2.txt`) and a 3-round, 4-CPU soak test (`soak.txt`).

- **Hardware & Gameplay Notes:**

- Untested on physical Master System hardware.

- High-budget CPU matches run ~5 seconds per turn as AI opponents stack shields and batteries; rounds cap at 200 turns (draw).

- Up to four tanks sharing the same scanline with active shields and parachutes will trigger the VDP's 8-sprites-per-scanline flicker limit.

- AI and Lazy Boy trajectory simulations treat Force Shields as solid targets rather than reflective surfaces.
